plain: The quality of being proper or fitting, in behavior or in action

webster.text: Property; peculiar or exclusive right of possession; ownership.

more.text: Fitness; suitableness; appropriateness; consonance with established principles, rules or customs; justness; accuracy.

example.quote: From these clear and indubitable principles results the propriety of a negative, either absolute or qualified, in the Executive, upon the acts of the legislative branches.
